## Summary

Cohort review of 20 maintained DUFMech family records (1 updated in Cycle 2 Stage 2 for native Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 taxon grounding and 18 updated in Cycle 2 Stage 3 for causal-graph protein-node grounding, plus PF01923, which together with PF01934 and PF01982 carries newly identified open causal-graph protein-grounding findings). All 20 families retain distinct Pfam boundaries and assay-separated causal graphs; 3 actionable protein-grounding findings remain open for Stage 5 grouped remediation.

## Scientific And Domain Assessments

### Cohort family boundaries and separated assay causal graphs

scope: supported. Targets: PF01062, PF01345, PF01535, PF01638, PF01709, PF01895, PF01910, PF01918, PF01923, PF01927, PF01930, PF01934, PF01938, PF01940, PF01973, PF01978, PF01980, PF01982, PF01984, PF02583.

All 20 reviewed Pfam families represent distinct evolutionary domains and biochemical or cellular mechanisms. Cycle 2 Stage 2 taxon grounding on PF01973 and Stage 3 protein-node UniProtKB groundings across 18 overlays preserve exact tested organism and construct scope without cross-species or cross-assay overreach.

### Open causal-graph protein-node grounding gaps in PF01923, PF01934, and PF01982

representation: concern. Targets: PF01923, PF01934, PF01982.

Three overlays in the cohort have unambiguous single-protein mappings in family_mapping that are missing on specific causal-graph nodes: PF01923 (sepduo-inhibition-2004 and sepduo-metal-additions-2004 missing UniProtKB:Q8ZNR5 on activity; seeutt-metal-oxygen-2014 missing UniProtKB:Q9ZFV4 on activity), PF01934 (fhepta-fragment-native-cfu-2026 missing paired UniProtKB:Q8EGZ7 alongside RefSeq:WP_164925653.1 on fragment; cleavage readout nodes in fhepta-fragment-rna-redox-2026 and so3166-modified-preparation-rnase-2020 missing protein grounding), and PF01982 (pyrbkr-flavin-binding-2017 and pyrbkr-temperature-response-2017 missing GenBank:AKT35049.1 on readout nodes; myrbkr-effector-binding-2017 missing UniProtKB:H2C8H2 on ribb/ribt readout nodes).

## Findings

### pf01923-sepduo-and-seeutt-assays-missing-protein-grounding: Ground Salmonella enterica PduO and EutT AdoCbl-forming activity nodes in sepduo-inhibition-2004, sepduo-metal-additions-2004, and seeutt-metal-oxygen-2014

minor / open / confirmed; issue key: pf01923-sepduo-and-seeutt-assays-missing-protein-grounding.

In curation/families/PF01923.yaml, three causal graphs have zero grounded protein nodes even though family_mapping explicitly maps the tested enzyme to a verified Salmonella enterica LT2 (NCBITaxon:99287) UniProtKB accession in evidence/PF01923/identity.txt: sepduo-inhibition-2004 (activity: AdoCbl-forming activity, lines 335-337) and sepduo-metal-additions-2004 (activity: AdoCbl-forming activity, lines 420-422) omit grounding: [UniProtKB:Q8ZNR5] (S. enterica LT2 PduO STM2050, UniProtKB:Q8ZNR5), whereas sibling graphs sepduo-truncation-activity-2004 and sepduo-triphosphate-2004 ground PduO activity to UniProtKB:Q8ZNR5; and seeutt-metal-oxygen-2014 (activity: Coupled AdoCbl-forming activity, lines 1207-1209) omits grounding: [UniProtKB:Q9ZFV4] (S. enterica LT2 EutT STM2456, UniProtKB:Q9ZFV4), whereas sibling graph seeutt-variant-activity-2014 grounds EutT perturbations to UniProtKB:Q9ZFV4.

### pf01934-fhepta-native-cfu-uniprot-grounding-and-cleavage-nodes: Add paired UniProtKB:Q8EGZ7 grounding to fhepta-fragment-native-cfu-2026 and ground FhepTA/HepT RNA-cleavage readout nodes

minor / open / confirmed; issue key: pf01934-fhepta-native-cfu-uniprot-grounding-and-cleavage-nodes.

In curation/families/PF01934.yaml (lines 585-603), graph fhepta-fragment-native-cfu-2026 (title: Fusion HEPN fragment lowers colony recovery in MR-1) grounds node fragment (Induce FhepTA136-276 rather than vector) only to [RefSeq:WP_164925653.1] and omits UniProtKB:Q8EGZ7, whereas sibling FhepTA136-276 graphs fhepta-fragment-ecoli-cfu-2026 (fragment, lines 558-563) and fhepta-fragment-rna-redox-2026 (reaction, lines 759-764) ground to [RefSeq:WP_164925653.1, UniProtKB:Q8EGZ7] per family_mapping (WP_164925653.1 fragment 136-276 contains the PF01934 core projected to 168-258 from Q8EGZ7v1 144-234). Additionally, the FhepTA136-276 and HepT RNase activity nodes fhepta-fragment-rna-redox-2026.nodes[3] (cleavage: MS2 RNA fragmentation by the isolated HEPN fragment, lines 771-773) and so3166-modified-preparation-rnase-2020.nodes[1] (cleavage: ompA RNA cleavage in the matched assay, lines 316-318) omit protein grounding ([RefSeq:WP_164925653.1, UniProtKB:Q8EGZ7] and [UniProtKB:Q8ECH6], respectively).

### pf01982-pyrbkr-effectors-and-temperature-grounding: Ground Pyrobaculum sp. WP30 pyRbkR flavin-binding and temperature-response assay readout nodes to GenBank:AKT35049.1 and myRbkR DNA-binding FP nodes to UniProtKB:H2C8H2

minor / open / confirmed; issue key: pf01982-pyrbkr-effectors-and-temperature-grounding.

In curation/families/PF01982.yaml (lines 705-812), the two Pyrobaculum sp. WP30 pyRbkR (GenBank:AKT35049.1) causal graphs pyrbkr-flavin-binding-2017 (fp: pyRbkR ribB-binding-associated FP, lines 723-725) and pyrbkr-temperature-response-2017 (activity: Relative FMN-producing activity in the temperature series, lines 778-780) omit grounding: [GenBank:AKT35049.1], leaving those two graphs with zero grounded protein nodes even though the two preceding pyRbkR graphs pyrbkr-fmn-production-2017 (reaction) and pyrbkr-target-binding-2017 (arfa_mix, arfa_complex, ribb_mix, ribb_complex) explicitly ground to [GenBank:AKT35049.1]. Similarly, in myrbkr-effector-binding-2017 (lines 616-640), the Methanocaldococcus vulcanius M7 myRbkR (UniProtKB:H2C8H2) DNA-binding readout nodes ribb (myRbkR ribB-binding-associated FP) and ribt (myRbkR ribT-binding-associated FP) omit grounding: [UniProtKB:H2C8H2].

## Recommended Actions And Acceptance Checks

### remediate-stage4-cohort-grounding-findings

In Stage 5 (resolve_review_findings), ground the Salmonella enterica PduO (UniProtKB:Q8ZNR5) and EutT (UniProtKB:Q9ZFV4) activity nodes in PF01923.yaml, add paired UniProtKB:Q8EGZ7 grounding to fhepta-fragment-native-cfu-2026 and ground the FhepTA/HepT RNA-cleavage readout nodes in PF01934.yaml, and ground the Pyrobaculum sp. WP30 pyRbkR (GenBank:AKT35049.1) and Methanocaldococcus vulcanius myRbkR (UniProtKB:H2C8H2) assay readout nodes in PF01982.yaml, recording canonical EDIT history events and regenerating projections.

- All three overlays record canonical EDIT history events and regenerate data/families/*.yaml cleanly.
- Every causal graph in PF01923, PF01934, and PF01982 has explicit protein grounding on its enzyme/fragment/readout nodes.
- just qc and kg_microbe_workflows validate-evidence pass.

## Category Boundaries

- retain: PF01062, PF01345, PF01535, PF01638, PF01709, PF01895, PF01910, PF01918, PF01923, PF01927, PF01930, PF01934, PF01938, PF01940, PF01973, PF01978, PF01980, PF01982, PF01984, PF02583. Each of the 20 Pfam entries is anchored to a distinct frozen InterPro/Pfam accession, structural fold, and experimental mechanism; none are redundant synonyms or chimeric family definitions warranting lumping or splitting. Within each family, biochemical, genetic, and reporter assays remain separated into distinct CausalGraph entries rather than lumped into unsupported multi-assay chains.

  kind: record_content
  reference: data/families/PF01062.yaml
  locator: dufmech-reviewed-projection-v1
  accessed_at: '2026-10-23T09:26:18Z'
  support: context_only
  snapshot_sha256: 926cb395039522bef961e9883f8139a966add427bfa2f2d000f4957a7a040402
  quote: "id: Pfam:PF01062\npfam_id: PF01062\nname: Bestrophin, RFP-TM, chloride channel\n\
    short_name: Bestrophin\nseed_status: EX_DUF\ncharacterization_status: UNSCORED\n\
    curation_status: IN_PROGRESS\nsource_url: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/api/entry/pfam/PF01062\n\
    counters:\n  proteins: 8246\n  matches: 8846\n  proteomes: 1318\n  taxa: 4218\n\
    \  structures: 45\n  alphafold_models: 7437\n  domain_architectures: 106\nprovenance:\n\
    \  snapshot_id: interpro-pfam-duf-2026-10-10\n  path: data/worklists/interpro-pfam-duf-2026-10-10.json\n\
    \  sha256: 17fb625876c9326ed284263a47bcd84e0d7844a31c040dc06cd2260c36f1c383\n\
    \  generated_at: '2026-10-10T07:44:21.614711Z'\n  source_url: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/api/entry/pfam/\n\
    interpro_id: InterPro:IPR021134\ndescription: This entry represents animal bestrophin\
    \ homologues. Bestrophin is a 68-kDa basolateral plasma\n  membrane protein expressed\
    \ in retinal pigment epithelial cells (RPE). It is encoded by the VMD2 gene,\n\
    \  which is mutated in Best macular dystrophy, a disease characterised by a depressed\
    \ light peak in the\n  electrooculogram [[cite:PUB00011865]]. VMD2 encodes a 585-amino\
    \ acid protein with an approximate mass\n  of 68 kDa which has been designated\
    \ bestrophin. Bestrophin shares homology with the Caenorhabditis elegans\n  RFP\
    \ gene family, named for the presence of a conserved arginine (R), phenylalanine\
    \ (F), proline (P),\n  amino acid sequence motif. Bestrophin is a plasma membrane\
    \ protein, localised to the basolateral surface\n  of RPE cells consistent with\
    \ a role for bestrophin in the generation or regulation of the EOG light\n  peak.\
    \ Bestrophin and other RFP family members represent a new class of chloride channels,\
    \ indicating\n  a direct role for bestrophin in generating the light peak [[cite:PUB00011865]].\
    \ The VMD2 gene underlying\n  Best disease was shown to represent the first human\
    \ member of the RFP-TM protein family. More than 97%\n  of the disease-causing\
    \ mutations are located in the N-terminal RFP-TM domain implying important functional\n\
    \  properties [[cite:PUB00011864]]. The bestrophins are four-pass transmembrane\
    \ chloride-channel proteins\n  [[cite:PUB00096747]], and the RFP-TM or bestrophin\
    \ domain extends from the N-terminus through approximately\n  350 amino acids\
    \ and contains all of the TM domains as well as nearly all reported disease causing\
    \ mutations\n  [[cite:PUB00109156]]. Interestingly, the RFP motif is not conserved\
    \ evolutionarily back beyond Metazoa,\n  neither is it in plant members.\ncuration_history:\
    \ history/records/PF01062\ndiscussions:\n- discussion_id: best1-gating-constructs-and-additional-contexts\n\
    \  prompt: Extend BEST1 gating and permeability contexts while preserving construct,\
    \ orientation and assay\n    differences.\n  kind: CURATION_TODO\n  status: OPEN\n\
    \  rationale: Purified current and coupled-flux effects do not directly resolve\
    \ every gating microstep\n    or establish a universal family mechanism. The tested\
    \ truncated region maps exactly despite full-length\n    differences between historical\
    \ and current references.\n  evidence:\n  - reference: PMID:27821745\n    supports:\
    \ PARTIAL\n    evidence_source: selected_full_text\n    explanation: Selected\
    \ primary Methods, Results and Figures 1/3/4 support eight edges. Aperture selectivity,\n\
    \      remaining substitutions and precise single-channel mechanisms need separately\
    \ scoped assessment.\n  posed_by: Codex\n  posed_date: '2026-10-11'\n  notes:\
    \ Resolve exact mutant clones, flux replicate/temperature details and incorporation\
    \ controls. Assess\n    later inactivation (PMID:30237227), cryo-EM gating (PMID:30628889)\
    \ and GABA activation (PMID:40249777)\n    as additional primary contexts, not\
    \ already reviewed edges. Do not transfer KpBest cation selectivity,\n    human\
    \ I205 numbering or structural-model trajectories. Partial same-agent scientific\
    \ review; remain\n    IN_PROGRESS.\ncausal_graphs:\n- graph_id: best1-bilateral-egta-current-loss\n\
    \  title: Bilateral calcium chelation decreases purified chicken BEST1 current\n\
    \  scope: Chicken BEST1 encoded residues 1-405 plus C-terminal EGEEF, expressed\
    \ in Pichia and reconstituted\n    in planar bilayers. Not the full 762-aa protein,\
    \ human retinal cells or bacterial KpBest.\n  context: 2016 Figure 1B-D representative\
    \ same-bilayer comparison. Symmetric 30 mM KCl, 20 mM HEPES-NaOH\n    pH 7.6,\
    \ 0.21 mM EGTA and 0.19 mM CaCl2 initially give about 300 nM free calcium; 3:1\
    \ wt/wt POPE/POPG,\n    22-24 C. Add 10 mM EGTA to both sides. Currents at +100\
    \ mV are averaged over the final 200 ms of a\n    2-s pulse; empty-bilayer currents\
    \ are subtracted.\n  family_mapping: Historical E1C3A0 is deleted, but its archived\
    \ sequence and current A0A8V0ZZU7 match\n    exactly at 1-405; PF01062 spans 1-324\
    \ inclusive. Five full-length differences lie beyond 405. PDB\n    4RDQ entity\
    \ 1 exactly matches current residues 2-405 plus EGEEF, consistent with the cited\
    \ purification's\n    MS/Edman-confirmed Thr2 start. Other mutant clone sequences\
    \ are not independently reconstructed.\n  scope_status: MECHANISTIC\n  taxon:\
    \ NCBITaxon:9031\n  limitations: This is a direct current endpoint after chelation,\
    \ not an observed atomic gate-closing\n    trajectory. Both channel orientations\
    \ are present; bilateral chelation is not interchangeable with\n    one-sided\
    \ treatment. The construct extends beyond the Pfam profile and does not prove\
    \ isolated-domain\n    sufficiency or a universal family calcium threshold.\n\
    \  nodes:\n  - node_id: bilateral-egta-in-wt-bilayer\n    label: Add 10 mM EGTA\
    \ to both sides of the WT BEST1 bilayer\n    node_type: PERTURBATION\n    grounding:\n\

    interpro_id: InterPro:IPR001434\ndescription: This entry, previously known as\
    \ DUF11, represents the CLIPPER domain, (Cross-Linked IsoPeptide\n  Protein in\
    \ the Extracellular Region) which is usually found in multiple copies in a number\
    \ of archaebacterial\n  proteins. CLIPPER domain adopts an Ig-like fold and contains\
    \ a conserved N-terminal lysine and a C-terminal\n  asparagine with central aspartate/glutamate\
    \ residues that form an intramolecular isopeptide bond [[cite:PUB00163642]].\n\
    \  The positions of the residues predicted to form isopeptide bonds are not universally\
    \ conserved suggesting\n  that some domains appear to lack the intramolecular\
    \ isopeptide bonds. CLIPPER domains are found in proteins\n  from Gram-positive\
    \ and Gram-negative bacteria. Some have also been identified in multiple cell-surface\n\
    \  proteins from archaea. In Methanothermobacter sp. CaT2, this domain plays a\
    \ key role as a membrane-bound\n  adhesion protein in the aggregation of CaT2\
    \ [[cite:PUB00097782]].\ncuration_history: history/records/PF01345\ndiscussions:\n\
    - discussion_id: clipper-residue-labels-and-native-contexts\n  prompt: Reconcile\
    \ residue labels and biochemical processing, and test transfer from a purified\
    \ repeat\n    to native CLIPPER-bearing proteins.\n  kind: CURATION_TODO\n  status:\
    \ OPEN\n  rationale: Table S6 and 9IFR resolve the intended fragment, but do not\
    \ validate the proposed catalytic\n    Asp748 label or every biochemical aliquot.\
    \ Three measured substitution effects do not establish native\n    adhesion, force\
    \ response, bond-formation kinetics or a shared function across all repeats.\n\
    \  evidence:\n  - reference: PMID:41236442\n    supports: PARTIAL\n    evidence_source:\
    \ full_text_and_supplement\n    explanation: Figures 5/6/S8 were visually inspected\
    \ and Table S6 coding sequences translated. K715A\n      is the only encoded protein\
    \ change; N748/D749 conflicts with the proposed Asp748 label. Raw diffraction\n\
    \      and biophysical data were not reanalyzed.\n  - reference: PMID:31189768\n\
    \    supports: PARTIAL\n    evidence_source: selected_full_text\n    explanation:\
    \ Selected CaT2 Results and Discussion distinguish whole MTCT_1020 aggregation\
    \ from domain-specific\n      DUF11 causality. Other regions or full-protein architecture\
    \ remain alternative explanations; no\n      archaeal edge is imported here.\n\
    \  posed_by: Codex\n  posed_date: '2026-10-11'\n  notes: Obtain experimental clone/tag\
    \ records and reconciled residue numbering; examine additional bacterial\n   \
    \ and archaeal members with their own interventions. Comparative absence of aggregation\
    \ is not a universal\n    negative. Partial scientific self-review; IN_PROGRESS.\n\
    causal_graphs:\n- graph_id: asilvestris-clipper-k715a-thermal-unfolding\n  title:\
    \ K715A lowers the CLIPPER fragment's thermal transition temperature\n  scope:\
    \ Purified synthetic B9T28_05395 residues 708-828 from Acinetobacter silvestris\
    \ ANC4999 in Costa\n    2025; a single repeat, not the full adhesin or all CLIPPER\
    \ domains.\n  context: Compare WT with K715A by circular dichroism during heating\
    \ from 5 to 95 C in 5-C increments.\n    Samples contain 0.36 mg/ml WT or 0.38\
    \ mg/ml mutant in 10 mM sodium phosphate, 100 mM sodium fluoride,\n    pH 7.4;\
    \ 300 ul in a 1-mm cuvette. Spectra span 180-280 nm and average four repeat scans.\
    \ pOPINF/BL21(DE3)\n    constructs were purified by nickel affinity and SEC; tag\
    \ removal is explicit for crystallography,\n    not unambiguously for these aliquots.\n\
    \  family_mapping: UniProtKB:A0A1Y3CHT7, B9T28_05395, is 2129 aa, sequence version\
    \ 1. Its sequence matches\n    InterPro; the tested PF01345 match is 712-812 within\
    \ the 708-828 construct. Table S6 WT DNA translates\n    exactly to that 121-aa\
    \ segment; mutant DNA differs only at K715A. Deposited 9IFR polymer is GP plus\n\

    interpro_id: InterPro:IPR002885\ndescription: This repeat has no known function.\
    \ It is about 35 amino acids long and found in up to 18\n  copies in some proteins.\
    \ This family appears to be greatly expanded in plants. This repeat occurs in\n\
    \  PET309 [swissprot:P32522] that may be involved in RNA stabilisation [[cite:PUB00001271]].\
    \ This domain\n  occurs in crp1 that is involved in RNA processing [[cite:PUB00001258]].\
    \ This repeat is associated with\n  a predicted plant protein [swissprot:O49549]\
    \ that has a domain organisation similar to the human BRCA1\n  protein. The repeat\
    \ has been called PPR [[cite:PUB00017589]].\ncuration_history: history/records/PF01535\n\

    interpro_id: InterPro:IPR048300\ndescription: This is a family of transcriptional\
    \ regulators. In mammals, it activates the transcription\n  of mitochondrially-encoded\
    \ COX1 [[cite:PUB00057436]]. In bacteria, it negatively regulates the quorum-sensing\n\
    \  response regulator by binding to its promoter region [[cite:PUB00057437]].\
    \ This entry represents the\n  second and third domains in this protein, with\
    \ one domain nested within the other.\ncuration_history: history/records/PF01709\n\
    discussions:\n- discussion_id: taco1-translation-not-transcription-and-domain-scope\n\

    \ mouse\n    and human experiments concern translation; the2024 profiling evidence\
    \ further qualifies older initiation\n    models. Current PF01709 covers the second/third\
    \ domains, not all of mature TACO1 or historical DUF28.\n  evidence:\n  - reference:\

    interpro_id: InterPro:IPR026022\ndescription: This family contains phosphate regulatory\
    \ proteins including PhoU. PhoU proteins are known\n  to play a role in the regulation\
    \ of phosphate uptake. The PhoU domain is composed of a three helix bundle\n \
    \ [[cite:PUB00031207]]. The PhoU protein contains two copies of this domain. The\
    \ domain binds to an iron\n  cluster via its conserved E/DXXXD motif.\ncuration_history:\
    \ history/records/PF01895\ndiscussions:\n- discussion_id: phou-chemical-and-interface-uncertainty\n\
    \  prompt: Resolve metal, phosphate and partner-interaction mechanisms without\
    \ promoting reporter effects\n    or models to atomic causal steps.\n  kind: CURATION_TODO\n\
    \  status: OPEN\n  rationale: E. coli Mn-probe data and mycobacterial net RegX3\
    \ phosphorylation support distinct experimentally\n    scoped effects. Neither\
    \ establishes universal iron occupancy, direct Pi binding, a PhoU phosphatase\n\
    \    active site, or inhibition of SenX3 autophosphorylation. Whole proteins carry\
    \ two PF01895 repeats,\n    and mutations can affect folding or abundance.\n \
    \ evidence:\n  - reference: PMID:24563032\n    supports: PARTIAL\n    evidence_source:\
    \ primary_methods_results_and_original_figures\n    explanation: Figure5 probe/dose\
    \ limits, Figure6 plasmid-versus-integrant distinction and Figure7 qualitative\n\
    \      fractionation are retained. Unavailable supplementary Mg/SEC curves and\
    \ the coelution condition\n      discrepancy need inspection.\n  - reference:\
    \ PMID:25953406\n    supports: PARTIAL\n    evidence_source: primary_methods_results_and_original_figures\n\
    \    explanation: Separate AP, growth and BACTH results prevent a uniform loss-of-function\
    \ claim. DCA/docking\n      remains a hypothesis; Figure5B omits R148E. Figure2\
    \ medium discrepancy and exact fusion orientation/dose\n      need resolution.\n\
    \  - reference: PMID:40588129\n    supports: PARTIAL\n    evidence_source: primary_methods_results_and_original_figures\n\
    \    explanation: PhoU1/Pi alters net RegX3 phosphorylation without reducing SenX3\
    \ autophosphorylation.\n      Direct Pi binding, a predicted alpha6 site and the\
    \ balance of phosphotransfer versus phosphatase\n      activities need discriminating\
    \ biochemical tests.\n  posed_by: Codex\n  posed_date: '2026-10-11'\n  notes:\
    \ Recover supplements, verify constructs and matched protein concentrations, assay\
    \ occupancy and\n    isolated reaction rates, and retain negative/condition-dependent\
    \ results. Do not draw metal-to-membrane-to-kinase\n    arrows by joining distinct\
    \ assays. Exact references and the access audit are retained under evidence/PF01895.\n\
    - discussion_id: phou-family-and-species-coverage\n  prompt: Extend the evidence\
    \ review to other PhoU members and physiological contexts without merging\n  \
    \  PF01865/PitR into PF01895.\n  kind: CURATION_TODO\n  status: OPEN\n  rationale:\
    \ Three mapped reference proteins in two species do not establish the mechanism\
    \ of24850 frozen\n    proteins. E. coli combined PstSCAB/PhoU reconstitution and\
    \ M. smegmatis PstB-deficient overexpression\n    are different conditions, not\
    \ interchangeable requirements or a controlled contradiction.\n  evidence:\n \
    \ - reference: PMID:19047379\n    supports: PARTIAL\n    evidence_source: selected_primary_transport_assay\n\
    \    explanation: Whole-cell uptake is curated; additional growth, suppressor,\
    \ mutant and long-term accumulation\n      contexts remain unreviewed or reported\
    \ without shown data.\n  - reference: doi:10.71150/jm.2505013\n    supports: PARTIAL\n\
    \    evidence_source: abstract_lead_only\n    explanation: Salmonella signaling/polyphosphate/virulence\
    \ claims require full assay review and exact\n      member mapping before graph\
    \ transfer.\n  - reference: PMID:42017666\n    supports: PARTIAL\n    evidence_source:\
    \ related_pf01865_review_and_final_publication_lead\n    explanation: The final\
    \ S. aureus publication replaces its preprint; conventional PhoU and PitR require\n\
    \      separate identities and allele scopes, and reused experiments are not independent\
    \ replications.\n  posed_by: Codex\n  posed_date: '2026-10-11'\n  notes: Review\
    \ mycobacterial2017 paralog phenotypes, conventional S. aureus PhoU, other structural\
    \ homologs\n    and persistence/virulence studies. Preserve imported identities/counters\
    \ and the graphless state of\n    unreviewed families. This is partial same-agent\
    \ scientific curation, not exhaustive family coverage,\n    independent endorsement\
    \ or publication.\ncausal_graphs:\n- graph_id: ec-phou-uptake\n  title: Loss of\
    \ PhoU increases cellular phosphate uptake\n  scope: Rice2009 Figure7; BM263 delta-phoU\

    interpro_id: InterPro:IPR002767\ndescription: The crystal structure of two of\
    \ these members shows that this domain has a ferredoxin like\n  fold and is likely\
    \ to exists as at least homodimers. Sulphate ions are are located at the dimer\
    \ interfaces,\n  which are thought to confer additional stability. Although the\
    \ function of this domain remains to be\n  identified, its structure suggests\
    \ a role in protein-protein interactions possibly regulated by the\n  binding\
    \ of small-molecule ligands [[cite:PUB00019479]]. Solution of the structure of\
    \ the hyperthermophilic\n  anaerobic Thermotoga maritima sequence, UniProtKB:Q9WYV6,\
    \ shows that this has a beta-alpha-beta-beta-alpha-beta\n  ferredoxin-like fold\
    \ and assembles as a homotetramer. It was possible to identify a pocket in each\
    \ monmer\n  that bound an unidentified ligand. It was also found that it bound\
    \ charged thiamine though not hydroxymethyl\n  pyrimidine. It is proposed that\
    \ it is transporting charged thiamine around the cytoplasm. Under oxidative\n\
    \  conditions this bacterium is under stress, and the transcriiptional unit within\
    \ which this protein is\n  expressed is up-regulated in these conditions, suggesting\
    \ that the chelation of cytoplasmic thaimine\n  is part of the response mechanism\
    \ to such oxidatvie stress, which is mediated by this family [[cite:PUB00055842]].\n\

    \ The reported association-constant\n    units are not reinterpreted.\n  nodes:\n\

    - graph_id: pfalba3-pat-sir2-assays-2023\n  title: Acetylation and Sir2 treatments\

    \ protein.\n  context: Acetylation:20 ug PfAlba3,5 ug SSO2813 Pat plus acetyl-CoA,20\
    \ ul10 mM Tris pH8/150 mM NaCl,65\n    C/1h. AP28 assay in SupplementS5C at37\
    \ C/1h. Deacetylation:10 ug each protein,50 ul50 mM Tris pH8/4\n    mM MgCl2/0.2\
    \ mM DTT,37 C/2h; published Methods prints500 mM NAD+, an unresolved unit issue.\n\
    \  family_mapping: P. falciparum 3D7 PfAlba3 Q8IJX8 sequence version 1, PF3D7_1006200\

    \ microsteps.\n  scope_status: MECHANISTIC\n  taxon: NCBITaxon:36329\n  limitations:\

    \ nuclease\n    activity. Colocalization is not an intracellular causal interaction.\

    \ mM DTT,37 C,4-6h\n    (introductory Methods says6h); NAD20/100/500 uM. Each\
    \ edge uses the joint enzyme/NAD reaction and\n    its minus-NAD control.\n  family_mapping:\

    interpro_id: InterPro:IPR016030\ndescription: Cobalamin adenosyltransferase This\
    \ family contains the gene products of PduO and EutT which\n  are both cobalamin\
    \ adenosyltransferases. PduO is a protein with ATP:cob(I)alamin adenosyltransferase\n\
    \  activity. The main role of this protein is the conversion of inactive cobalamins\
    \ to AdoCbl for 1,2-propanediol\n  degradation [[cite:PUB00013593]].The EutT enzyme\
    \ appears to be an adenosyl transferase, converting CNB12\n  to AdoB12 [[cite:PUB00009955]].\n\

    \  generated_at: '2026-10-10T07:44:21.614711Z'\n  source_url: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/api/entry/pfam/\n\
    interpro_id: InterPro:IPR008201\ndescription: This family includes the toxic component\
    \ HepT of a type II toxin-antitoxin (TA) system, which\n  has RNase activity.\
    \ These proteins contain a HEPN (higher eukaryotes and prokaryotes nucleotide-binding)\n\
    \  domain and are neutralised through tri-AMPylation by the cognate antitoxin\
    \ MntA, containing a MNT (minimal\n  nucleotidyltransferase) domain [[cite:PUB00097221],[cite:PUB00097219],[cite:PUB00097220]].\
    \ HepT-MnA\n  form an heterooctamer (at a 2:6 ratio), a rare organisation for\
    \ this kind of TA systems. HepT dimerises\n  and enables the formation of a deep\
    \ cleft at the HEPN-domain interface, containing the RX4-6H motif\n  (where X\
    \ is any amino acid and the residue immediately after the conserved R is typically\
    \ a polar amino\n  acid) as the active site that functions as an RNA-cleaving\
    \ RNase. This type II TA system regulates cell\n  motility and confers plasmid\
    \ stability [[cite:PUB00097219]]. Due to the prevalence of these HEPN/MNT\n  modules\
    \ in bacteria and archaea, it has been suggested that these TA systems may also\
    \ play a role in\n  the environmental adaptation to extreme habitats [[cite:PUB00097220]].\n\

    interpro_id: InterPro:IPR002794\ndescription: Members of this family have several\
    \ predicted transmembrane helices. One member of the family\n  has been characterised\
    \ as protein PGR (AtPGR). PGR is suggested to be a potential glucose-responsive\n\
    \  regulator in carbohydrate metabolism in plants. This entry also includes protein\
    \ VTE6, which is a Pphytyl-phosphate\n  kinase catalysing the conversion of phytyl-monophosphate\
    \ to phytyl-diphosphate [[cite:PUB00092523]].\ncuration_history: history/records/PF01940\n\

    interpro_id: InterPro:IPR002826\ndescription: This domain can be found in a group\
    \ of proteins, including archaeal 6-hydroxymethylpterin\n  diphosphokinase (6-HMDPK),\
    \ known as MptE, which catalyses the formation of 6-hydroxymethyl-7,8-dihydropterin\n\
    \  diphosphate (6-HMDP) from 6-HMD and ATP [[cite:PUB00061602]]. 6-HMDP is the\
    \ precursor of the pterin\n  containing moiety of the essential C1-carriers tetrahydrofolate\
    \ and tetrahydromethanopterin. This entry\n  also includes a number of uncharacterised\
    \ proteins from bacteria.\ncuration_history: history/records/PF01973\ndiscussions:\n\
    - discussion_id: mpte-substrates-and-constructs\n  prompt: Resolve archaeal substrate\
    \ breadth, constructs and catalytic steps beyond the reported assays.\n  kind:\

    \ substrate or native archaeal flux.\n  evidence:\n  - reference: PMID:22931285\n\
    \    supports: PARTIAL\n    evidence_source: primary_publication\n    explanation:\
    \ Original Figure 4 and Methods distinguish displayed PF0930 chemistry from reported\
    \ similar\n      MJ1634 activity and E. coli complementation. The supporting purity\
    \ gel concerns MJ1634.\n  posed_by: Codex\n  posed_date: '2026-10-14'\n  notes:\

    \ C purification\n    wording, test natural substrate breadth and catalytic residues,\
    \ and inspect later structural/biochemical\n    work. A monophosphate workup peak\
    \ is not a demonstrated enzyme step. See evidence/PF01973/crecy-2012-mpte.txt.\n\
    - discussion_id: maf-chemistry-versus-phenotypes\n  prompt: Resolve Maf donor\
    \ stereochemistry and distinguish residue chemistry from protein stability or\n\

  quote: "id: Pfam:PF01980\npfam_id: PF01980\nname: tRNA-methyltransferase O N-terminal\
    \ domain\nshort_name: TrmO_N\nseed_status: EX_DUF\ncharacterization_status: UNSCORED\n\
    curation_status: IN_PROGRESS\nsource_url: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/api/entry/pfam/PF01980\n\
    counters:\n  proteins: 8639\n  matches: 8684\n  proteomes: 7015\n  taxa: 12908\n\
    \  structures: 6\n  alphafold_models: 5968\n  domain_architectures: 76\nprovenance:\n\
    \  snapshot_id: interpro-pfam-duf-2026-10-10\n  path: data/worklists/interpro-pfam-duf-2026-10-10.json\n\
    \  sha256: 17fb625876c9326ed284263a47bcd84e0d7844a31c040dc06cd2260c36f1c383\n\
    \  generated_at: '2026-10-10T07:44:21.614711Z'\n  source_url: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/api/entry/pfam/\n\
    interpro_id: InterPro:IPR023370\ndescription: This family includes members such\
    \ as TrmO (tRNA-methyltransferase O) also known as YaeB,\n  which contains a single-sheeted\
    \ beta-barrel structure. TrmO is an AdoMet-dependent methyltransferase\n  responsible\
    \ for m6t6A formation [[cite:PUB00086552]]. Its human homolog, is responsible\
    \ for formation\n  of m6t6A37 in cytoplasmic tRNASer. Lack of TrmO decreases attenuation\
    \ activity of the thr operon, indicating\n  that N6 methylation of m6t6A37 ensures\
    \ efficient decoding of ACY codons [[cite:PUB00137799]]. In bacteria\n  and eukaryotes,\
    \ TrmO has a C-terminal domain containing the conserved DPRxxY motif. Where the\
    \ Asp194\n  and Arg196 in this motif of E. coli TrmO are necessary for N6-methylation.\
    \ However, no archaeal YaeB\n  has a C-terminal domain containing the DPRxxY motif\
    \ that is conserved in bacterial and mammalian TrmO\n  homologs [[cite:PUB00086552]].\
    \ This entry represents the N-terminal domain of TrmO.\ncuration_history: history/records/PF01980\n\

    \  sha256: 17fb625876c9326ed284263a47bcd84e0d7844a31c040dc06cd2260c36f1c383\n\
    \  generated_at: '2026-10-10T07:44:21.614711Z'\n  source_url: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/api/entry/pfam/\n\
    interpro_id: InterPro:IPR023602\ndescription: This domain is a CTP-dependent riboflavin\
    \ kinase (RFK), found in archaea, that catalyses\n  the phosphorylation of riboflavin\
    \ to form flavin mononucleotide in riboflavin biosynthesis [ec:2.7.1.26].\n  Its\
    \ structure resembles a RIFT barrel, structurally similar to but topologically\
    \ distinct from bacterial\n  and eukaryotic examples. The N-terminal is a winged\
    \ helix-turn-helix DNA-binding domain, and the C-terminal\n  half is most similar\
    \ in sequence to a group of cradle-loop barrels. [swissprot:O28174] has this domain\n\
    \  attached to [pfam:PF00325].\ncuration_history: history/records/PF01982\ndiscussions:\n\
    - discussion_id: ribk-donor-and-metal-discrepancies\n  prompt: Resolve nucleotide-donor\
    \ and metal dependence across the original RibK studies.\n  kind: CURATION_TODO\n\
    \  status: OPEN\n  rationale: The 2008 enzyme retains ATP/GTP activity and copurified\
    \ Mg; strict CTP-only and metal-independent\n    claims are not justified by these\
    \ assays.\n  evidence:\n  - reference: PMID:18245297\n    supports: PARTIAL\n\
    \    evidence_source: primary_publication\n    explanation: Equal-concentration\
    \ ATP/GTP yield 30%/11% of CTP activity; no-added-metal protein contains\n   \
    \   4-5 mol Mg per mol protein.\n  - reference: PMID:18073108\n    supports: PARTIAL\n\
    \    evidence_source: primary_publication\n    explanation: Abstract inspected\
    \ but original full text returned 403; IUBMB cites this study for lack\n     \
    \ of ATP/GTP use.\n  - reference: https://hdl.handle.net/10900/49675\n    supports:\
    \ PARTIAL\n    evidence_source: primary_publication\n    explanation: Ammelburg's\
    \ 2011 primary account supplies the original assay protocol and qualitative\n\
    \      donor contrasts; Figure9G retains a small FMN-labeled ATP peak despite\
    \ its negative caption.\n  posed_by: Codex\n  posed_date: '2026-10-16'\n  notes:\
    \ The 2011 dissertation is a primary account of the 2007 work, not independent\
    \ replication or verified\n    journal-text identity. Its assay contains 5 mM\
    \ MgCl2 without a metal-removal intervention. Different\n    constructs and assay\
    \ conditions do not establish why 2008 ATP/GTP activity differs. Original journal\n\
    \    text and donor-purity/metal controls remain follow-ups. EC2.7.1.161 is current\
    \ nomenclature; the frozen\n    EC2.7.1.26 description remains imported source\
    \ text, not curated chemistry.\n- discussion_id: rbkr-constructs-residues-and-physiology\n\
    \  prompt: Resolve exact constructs, causal residue roles and native regulatory\
    \ polarity without assigning\n    wHTH activity to PF01982 alone.\n  kind: CURATION_TODO\n\
    \  status: OPEN\n  rationale: Reference-domain annotations and static contacts\
    \ do not establish domain sufficiency, proton\n    transfer or native transcriptional\
    \ activation.\n  evidence:\n  - reference: PMID:28073944\n    supports: PARTIAL\n\
    \    evidence_source: primary_publication\n    explanation: Whole-fusion biochemical\
    \ assays and DNA-bound structure support distinct observations;\n      activation\
    \ and FMN-induced structural switching remain proposed.\n  - reference: https://hdl.handle.net/10900/49675\n\
    \    supports: PARTIAL\n    evidence_source: primary_publication\n    explanation:\
    \ Static apo and product complexes motivate an explicitly hypothetical ordered-binding\n\
    \      and E107 base model; no causal residue intervention was inspected.\n  posed_by:\
    \ Codex\n  posed_date: '2026-10-16'\n  notes: Archived A0A0K1E2F9 entry33 maps\
    \ AKT35049.1 to PF01982 at 88-208; the current entry is deleted.\n    Q60365 sequence2\
    \ postdates the original studies. The 136-aa archived Q60365 and 2P3M/2VBU/2VBV\
    \ references\n    have an MVKL prefix relative to current 132-aa Q60365; deposited\
    \ E107 maps to current E103 and PF01982\n    7-125 maps to deposited 11-129. The\
    \ prefix is not established as a vector tag. Verify physical inserts,\n    cleavage\
    \ junctions, folding/abundance and residue perturbations before stronger transfer.\n\

    interpro_id: InterPro:IPR003735\ndescription: This is a family of metal-sensitive\
    \ repressors, involved in resistance to metal ions. Members\n  of this family\
    \ bind copper, nickel or cobalt ions via conserved cysteine and histidine residues.\
    \ In\n  the absence of metal ions, these proteins bind to promoter regions and\
    \ repress transcription. When bound\n  to metal ions they are unable to bind DNA,\
    \ leading to transcriptional derepression [[cite:PUB00041403],[cite:PUB00057455],[cite:PUB00057456],[cite:PUB00057457],[cite:PUB00035608]].\n\
    curation_history: history/records/PF02583\ndiscussions:\n- discussion_id: csor-members-and-allosteric-limits\n\

    \ separate B. subtilis effects. The family\n    spans other regulators, and structural\
    \ allosteric steps, other promoters and metal specificity require\n    their own\
    \ experiments.\n  evidence:\n  - reference: PMID:19249860\n    supports: PARTIAL\n\
    \    evidence_source: full_text\n    explanation: Figure 7 was visually inspected.\
    \ The E90A result supports coupling but not a resolved\n      atomic pathway;\
    \ weak Ni/Zn coupling must not be recast as universally absent activity.\n  -\
    \ reference: PMID:18048925\n    supports: PARTIAL\n    evidence_source: full_text\n\
    \    explanation: Figure 2 and strain/reporter methods were inspected; complementation\
    \ supports the genetic\n      phenotype. The earlier YhdQ assignment is explicitly\
    \ corrected by this source.\n  posed_by: Codex\n  posed_date: '2026-10-11'\n \
    \ notes: No continuous observed chain from copper exposure through efflux and\
    \ growth is asserted. Raw\n    data, other family members, indirect ycnKJI regulation\
    \ and a complete structural mechanism remain\n    outside this partial review.\n\
    causal_graphs:\n- graph_id: bsub-csor-copper-operator-binding\n  title: Copper\
    \ loading reduces purified B. subtilis CsoR operator binding\n  scope: Intact\
    \ purified B. subtilis CsoR compared in apo and Cu(I)-loaded states on a synthetic\
    \ copZA\n    operator; not cellular transcription or an isolated PF02583 domain.\n\
    \  context: Figure 7A fluorescence anisotropy uses 4 nM labeled 30-bp operator\
    \ DNA, 10 mM MES, 0.4 M NaCl,\n    2 mM DTT, pH 6.5 and 25 C. Protein was expressed\
    \ in E. coli BL21(DE3) from a Helmann-laboratory pET16b\n    construct. Five readings\
    \ were averaged at each titration addition.\n  family_mapping: B. subtilis csoR,\
    \ formerly yvgZ, is BSU33520 and maps to UniProtKB:O32222, reference\n    sequence\
    \ version 1, 101 residues, PF02583 at 17-97. The assay uses intact protein, not\

    \  scope_status: MECHANISTIC\n  taxon: NCBITaxon:224308\n  limitations: The Cu-loaded\

    \ nanomolar assembly differences. No family-wide copper specificity, transcription\n\
    \    endpoint or cellular efflux is inferred.\n  nodes:\n  - node_id: csor-copper-loaded\n\

    - graph_id: bsub-csor-null-copza-reporter\n  title: Loss of csoR increases copZA\

    whereas sibling graphs sepduo-truncation-activity-2004 and sepduo-triphosphate-2004
    ground PduO activity to UniProtKB:Q8ZNR5; and seeutt-metal-oxygen-2014 (activity:
    Coupled AdoCbl-forming activity, lines 1207-1209) omits grounding: [UniProtKB:Q9ZFV4]
    (S. enterica LT2 EutT STM2456, UniProtKB:Q9ZFV4), whereas sibling graph seeutt-variant-activity-2014
    grounds EutT perturbations to UniProtKB:Q9ZFV4.'
